classification.difficultyReason: Select and combine the explicitly taught centre/circumference theorem, reflex-angle subtraction, equal-radii triangle sums and diameters across nine supplied diagrams. All goals are specified; the hardest case requires a short linked chain without a new construction.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, giving reasons.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, chords PA and PB, and radii OA and OB. Alpha is the lower central angle; 240 degrees labels its reflex counterpart.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=360^\circ-240^\circ\\\alpha&=120^\circ\\\beta&=\tfrac12\times120^\circ\\\beta&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles about a point sum to $360^\circ$. The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre standing on the same arc.

spec.description: Radii OA and OB and chords PA and PB; 300 degrees labels the reflex central sector.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=360^\circ-300^\circ\\\angle AOB&=60^\circ\\\theta&=\tfrac12\times60^\circ\\\theta&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
Use angles about a point, then the centre–circumference theorem on minor arc $AB$.

spec.description: Chords TS and TR and radii OS and OR; theta labels the reflex central sector to the left of O.
spec.mathematics: STR=70 degrees; theta is reflex SOR.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle SOR&=2\times70^\circ\\\angle SOR&=140^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-140^\circ\\\theta&=220^\circ\end{align*}$$
The minor central angle is twice $\angle STR$ on the same arc. Angles about $O$ sum to $360^\circ$.

spec.description: Both unknown circumference angles stand on arc FG; beta is identified by an external leader.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tfrac12\times80^\circ=40^\circ\\\beta&=\tfrac12\times80^\circ=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Each angle at the circumference stands on the same arc $FG$ as the $80^\circ$ central angle.

spec.description: Chords PS, PR, QS and QR and radii OS and OR; a leader gives angle SPR; theta labels reflex SOR.
spec.mathematics: SPR=20 degrees; alpha=SQR; theta is reflex SOR.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle SOR&=2\times20^\circ=40^\circ\\\theta&=360^\circ-40^\circ=320^\circ\\\alpha&=\tfrac12\times40^\circ=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Use the centre–circumference theorem on arc $SR$ and angles about $O$.

spec.description: Triangle PRQ with radii OP, OR and OQ; unknown central sectors alpha and beta and angle RPO labelled gamma.
spec.mathematics: POQ=120 degrees; ORQ=40 degrees; alpha=ROQ; beta=ROP; gamma=RPO.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$OR=OQ$, so $\angle OQR=40^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-40^\circ-40^\circ=100^\circ\\\beta&=360^\circ-120^\circ-100^\circ=140^\circ\\\gamma&=\frac{180^\circ-140^\circ}{2}=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Use the angle sum of $\triangle ROQ$, angles about $O$, and the equal base angles of $\triangle ROP$, where $OR=OP$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral BPAQ with radii OB and OA; alpha stands on the upper arc BA and gamma on the lower arc BA.
spec.mathematics: Minor BOA=160 degrees; beta is reflex BOA; alpha=BQA; gamma=BPA.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tfrac12\times160^\circ=80^\circ\\\beta&=360^\circ-160^\circ=200^\circ\\\gamma&=\tfrac12\times200^\circ=100^\circ\end{align*}$$
Each circumference angle is half the central angle standing on its arc. Angles about $O$ sum to $360^\circ$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral DABC with diameters AC and DB; source angle labels are retained on each side of the diameters.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$\angle DAB=90^\circ$ because $DB$ is a diameter.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ\\\beta&=\alpha=60^\circ\\\gamma&=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
$OA=OB$, so the base angles of $\triangle AOB$ are equal. Also $\angle ABC=90^\circ$ because $AC$ is a diameter.

spec.description: Quadrilateral JKLM with perpendicular diameters JL and KM; right-angle square constructed from the radius vectors OK and OL.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens and unknown labels only.

answer.worked:
$OJ=OK$ and $\angle JOK=90^\circ$, so $\triangle JOK$ is isosceles. Likewise $OK=OL$ and $\angle KOL=90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}=45^\circ\\\beta&=\frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
